title: Adentris vs JotPsych: Behavioral Health Documentation Compared
summary: Adentris vs JotPsych for behavioral health and SUD: an AI scribe with coding suggestions versus real-time revenue integrity, ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth, and an appeals and denials module.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** JotPsych and Adentris both work in behavioral health documentation, but they solve different halves of the problem. JotPsych is an AI scribe built exclusively for behavioral health that drafts structured notes from the session and adds coding suggestions and audit-risk flags. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note, however it was written, in real time before the claim is submitted, with SUD-specific rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals and denials module built in. If your problem is note-writing time, JotPsych is built for that. If your problem is denials and audit exposure, that is where Adentris focuses. They can work together.


Because they emphasize different jobs, the honest comparison is less about which is better and more about which problem you are solving right now. Here is the breakdown.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is not a scribe: it does not write the note, it makes sure the note will get paid. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What JotPsych does


JotPsych is an AI documentation platform built exclusively for behavioral health, covering psychiatry, psychology, therapy, and counseling. It drafts structured notes from session recordings or dictation using a large library of behavioral health note sections, and it embeds ICD-10, DSM-5-TR, and CPT coding suggestions along with audit-risk flags that highlight missing documentation elements. For practices that want a scribe designed from the ground up for mental health, with coding and reimbursement support built in, JotPsych is a strong, focused option.

## Where each fits


JotPsych is built to draft the behavioral health note and suggest the codes, with flags for missing elements inside that note. Adentris is built to review the finished documentation against payer and regulatory denial criteria before submission, whoever or whatever wrote it, and to draft the fix and support the appeal. For a SUD program, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and a paired appeals workflow, running on any EHR through a secure web agent. A practice can use JotPsych to write and code the note and Adentris to make sure it survives the payer.


## Adentris as a JotPsych alternative for revenue integrity and denials


If your program uses JotPsych, or is evaluating it, and the gap you feel is not note-writing time but denied claims and audit exposure, that is a different job. JotPsych flags audit risk inside the note it drafts; Adentris reviews the finished documentation against payer and regulatory denial criteria, drafts the correction before submission, and pairs that with an appeals and denials workflow. It runs on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent, so it fits alongside a behavioral health scribe or in place of a general compliance check. For programs that already write and code notes well but still lose claims, it is a natural complement or alternative.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. At Sobrius Health, a multi-site Virginia SUD provider, pre-submission documentation accuracy moved from 73% to 96%. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. ## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and JotPsych?**


JotPsych is an AI scribe built exclusively for behavioral health that drafts structured notes and suggests ICD-10, DSM-5-TR, and CPT codes, with audit-risk flags inside the note. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the finished note in real time before the claim is submitted, drafts corrections, and has SUD-specific rules like ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals module built in. JotPsych helps write and code the note; Adentris makes sure it gets paid.


**Can Adentris and JotPsych be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use JotPsych to draft and code the note and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside JotPsych.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to JotPsych?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than note-writing time and coding support, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. JotPsych is strong for behavioral health note drafting with coding suggestions. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
